LESSON: WRITING 10.4.1 PUNCTUATION (THE EXCLAMATION MARK)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Writing 10.4.1 Punctuation (The exclamation mark)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 10.4.1 Punctuation (The exclamation mark), part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: Why do you think it is important to use the exclamation mark when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 10.4.1 Punctuation (The exclamation mark) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration is enhanced as the learner plays games with peers that involve placing the exclamation mark correctly in a

text.

Values:
Respect as the learner plays games that involve placing the exclamation mark correctly in a text.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self-esteem) -as the learner uses exclamation mark correctly in writing.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The exclamation mark is learnt in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Wall charts, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital

devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
